reviews.text: My dog ​​had a tooth extraction, they gave him medication that made him sick and misdiagnosed him – terrible service!
The only ones who truly treat specialties as such, great service.
Dr. Emilio, a specialist ophthalmologist and veterinarian, is one of the best.

Some things could be improved, like sending the report I requested several times faster, but it was finally sent, and most importantly: they saved my baby's life. This is something I will never forget and is far more important than any delay in processing a file. I have no words to thank them for what they did for my dog; he is with me now thanks to the professionals at this center. I highly recommend them for any emergency, vaccinations, deworming, and travel paperwork abroad. Thank you for everything!

I've been taking Leah (a female pit bull) to this clinic for six years, and they've always been professional, polite, and empathetic. I think it's incredibly important that people have that kind of tact because of the delicate situations that can arise. 100% recommended for bathing, vaccinations, diagnostics, and emergencies. No price gouging or excessive wait times.

It's so sad to see how right on the street where this veterinary hospital is located there are so many stray dogs, and they can't receive any kind of care simply because of their love for their profession: whether it's contacts for adoption centers, spaying/neutering, and more for the strays that no one cares for! We understand that this involves some minimal expense for supplies, but there are many solutions: collecting donations from people in the area to help them, advertising, etc. And considering that their services are more expensive than average, it wouldn't hurt them to do a good deed. I hope they'll consider doing a good deed for the animals in the area, since they have the necessary resources <3!

I had a profoundly painful experience at this veterinary clinic. I took my dog ​​there hoping she would receive professional care, but instead, I found care focused primarily on generating revenue for the hospital.

During her hospitalization, the medical care was ambiguous, the diagnoses uncertain, and the expenses piled up without clarity or empathy.

The bills were exorbitant, and if I hadn't been vigilant, they would have even charged me for another patient's expenses by mistake. "A $7,000 error."

I believe they unnecessarily extended her treatment without clearly explaining the true prognosis, which only prolonged my dog's suffering and caused me emotional distress.

They led me to believe there was hope when they probably already knew there was no turning back. I would have preferred to request euthanasia rather than watch her waste away. But that wouldn't have been profitable for the hospital.

Some staff members displayed an arrogant and indifferent attitude, which made an already devastating process even more difficult.

Communication with receptionists and doctors is neither clear nor efficient. I can't say the same about Dr. Alan, who honestly treated me and my dog ​​well.

Looking back on the situation now that it's calmer, I think my dog's suffering could have been avoided if only they had prioritized ethics over admission.

I wouldn't return, nor would I recommend it. In moments like these, you need humanity, not just a receipt.
